dedupe_keys.name: fhwa regional assessment of weather impacts on freight 13 us regions

description: This Federal Highway Administration report (FHWA-HOP-16-044, February 2016), written by Daniel Krechmer, Noel Perry and colleagues at Cambridge Systematics, CASE Consultants International and Transport Fundamentals, follows a 2012 national estimate that weather-related delay costs the trucking industry $8 billion to $9 billion a year with a more detailed look at 13 diverse urban and rural regions. Coverage: selected major highway segments in 13 US regions, using truck travel times from the National Performance Management Research Data Set and weather observations such as the Automated Surface Observing System. Weather events significantly reduce traffic speeds, and so harm freight, at regional level; on the limited set of highways studied, the lost speed costs the freight industry an estimated $3.8 million a year. Ice, snow, fog, heavy rain, wind and extreme temperatures were most correlated with lower speeds, with the biggest drops in the first hour of storms and stronger effects in peak hours. Format and access: a 72-page PDF. Licence and cost: a US Government report, free with no distribution restrictions. Caveats: segment-level results do not cover whole networks. The speed reductions by weather type can be used as link capacity or speed factors when simulating freight network flows under weather hazards. It relates to the Freight Analysis Framework and the FHWA Urban Congestion Reports in the catalogue.
